stem: A client has an elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) result. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: LDH is widely distributed in body tissues and can rise in many disorders, so an elevated value is nonspecific and must be interpreted with the clinical context.
options.B: An elevated LDH level identifies one specific malignancy and can establish a cancer diagnosis without other diagnostic evidence.
options.C: LDH elevation primarily indicates kidney disease and has little relevance to disorders involving the liver, blood, muscle, lung, or heart.
options.D: An elevated LDH level establishes acute myocardial infarction and can substitute for contemporary cardiac troponin testing.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance states that LDH is present in all cells, with high concentrations in the heart, liver, muscle, kidney, lung, and erythrocytes, and that serum LDH is elevated in numerous clinical conditions. Mayo notes that LDH elevations in cancer are too erratic for cancer diagnosis and that LDH has been replaced by troponin for myocardial-infarction assessment. Therefore A is correct; B, C, and D each make an unsupported disease-specific conclusion.
educational_objective: Interpret elevated LDH as a nonspecific marker associated with injury or disease in multiple tissues rather than as a stand-alone diagnosis.
source_version_date: Current Mayo test catalog; test-definition document generated February 12, 2026; live page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Useful For: investigation of diseases involving heart, liver, muscle, kidney, lung, and blood; LDH elevations in cancer too erratic for diagnosis. Clinical Information/Interpretation: LDH widely distributed and elevated in many conditions. Cautions: LDH after MI has been replaced by troponin.
source_claim_supported: Serum LDH elevation is nonspecific across many tissues and diseases and does not independently diagnose cancer or myocardial infarction.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor and interpret diagnostic/laboratory findings.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only 'only' wording and balanced all alternatives as parallel interpretations of elevated LDH.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current Mayo guidance explicitly documents broad tissue distribution, multiple causes, poor cancer diagnostic specificity, and replacement by troponin for MI; A uniquely matches.
